regulates: [GAP-PASS CRITICAL VALIDATION] TEAD-1 is reported as a VEZF1 binding partner at a shared MCAT element in the Myh7/beta-MHC promoter -- this is a co-occupancy/binding-partner claim, NOT a demonstrated regulatory (X-controls-VEZF1) relationship in either direction.
evidence_direction: Evidence-type classification (per the six-category scheme: A=direct biochemical interaction, B=co-occupancy, C=transcriptional regulation, D=genetic perturbation, E=drug perturbation, F=correlation only): the paper's own wording ('TEAD-1 is a binding partner of Vezf1') places this claim at (A)/(B) -- direct interaction or co-occupancy at one specific promoter site. [CORRECTED after Codex full-text review, which located PMC6948172]: TEAD1 WAS experimentally perturbed in the paper -- neonatal/adult rat ventricular cardiomyocytes were transfected with two distinct TEAD1 siRNAs (Methods), and TEAD1 knockdown was used in Fig. 6F to confirm the specificity of the ~40-kDa TEAD1 band in a co-immunoprecipitation experiment. HOWEVER this TEAD1 knockdown was used ONLY as an antibody/band-specificity control -- the paper does not report measuring VEZF1 expression, VEZF1 activity, or the Myh7-promoter response AFTER TEAD1 knockdown. So while category (D) genetic perturbation of TEAD1 DID occur in this study, it was not used to test whether TEAD1 is required for VEZF1's regulatory effect -- there is still no reported experiment measuring a TEAD1-perturbation-to-VEZF1-output relationship. Category (E) drug perturbation was not attempted.
perturbation_type: TEAD1 WAS knocked down (siRNA, rat cardiomyocytes) but only as a co-IP antibody-specificity control, NOT to test a TEAD1->VEZF1 functional relationship (see evidence_direction; corrected after Codex full-text review of PMC6948172). No perturbation experiment measuring VEZF1 output after TEAD1 knockdown was reported. A dedicated PubMed search this pass for '(TEAD1 AND VEZF1)' returns EXACTLY ONE result in the entirety of PubMed: PMID 31911272 itself (NCBI esearch, live query, confirmed 2026-08-14, count=1). No other paper, in any species or context, has ever studied TEAD1 and VEZF1 together. A further search for 'TEAD1 AND (breast OR ER-positive OR estrogen receptor OR tamoxifen)' returns 39 results, but NONE of them involve VEZF1 -- they establish TEAD1's independent relevance to estrogen-receptor biology in OTHER contexts (e.g. PMID 42050304: TEAD1 binds the ERalpha promoter in an osteogenesis context; PMID 40500464: estrogen-receptor activation remodels TEAD1 expression in a hepatic-steatosis context) but say nothing about VEZF1 and are not evidence for this specific hypothesis.
cancer_context: NONE for the TEAD1-VEZF1 relationship specifically -- the source biology (PMID 31911272) is cardiac/zebrafish, not oncology, and no breast-cancer, ER+, or mammary-epithelium study connecting TEAD1 to VEZF1 was identified in the searches performed.
druggability: [GAP-PASS CORRECTION to the prior pass's framing] TEAD1 IS druggable, but the prior pass overstated this as a clean 'TEAD1-specific clinical-stage chemotype.' The actual picture: VT3989 (a real, active Phase 1/2 clinical compound, FDA Fast Track for mesothelioma/NF2-mutated solid tumors) is a PAN-TEAD auto-palmitoylation-pocket inhibitor -- it blocks TEAD1-4 collectively, NOT TEAD1 selectively. IK-930, which WAS a TEAD1-selective palmitate-pocket inhibitor, had its clinical program DISCONTINUED after a review of clinical data showing only modest activity. No compound with confirmed TEAD1-only selectivity remains in active clinical development as of the searches performed. Real ChEMBL entries exist (CHEMBL3334416 direct TEAD1; CHEMBL3430909 YAP1/TEAD1 PPI; CHEMBL6066051 cereblon/TEAD1 PPI; CHEMBL6195504 VHL/TEAD1 PPI) confirming TEAD1 is a chemically tractable target in principle.
existing_inhibitor: YES for pan-TEAD (VT3989, active Phase 1/2). The TEAD1-selective compound (IK-930) was discontinued. No breast-cancer or ER+ clinical evidence for either compound was identified in the searches performed.
normal_tissue_concern: not independently assessed this pass -- TEAD1/Hippo-pathway inhibition has its own normal-tissue biology (Hippo signaling is broadly important in tissue growth control) that would need its own dedicated review before any recommendation; explicitly flagged as outstanding.
project_evidence: TEAD1 is independently significant in this project's own resistance-RNA datasets -- GSE118713 log2FC=-0.935, FDR=0.0151 (down in TAMR); GSE240112 tumor log2FC=-0.996, FDR=0.0464 (down in tumor, direction agreement=True); GSE245601 epithelial track p=0.0499 (nominal only, FDR=0.358, not significant); GSE111151 FDR=0.967 (no signal); Hany CRISPR effect=-0.397, FDR=0.801 (not significant, sensitising_KO direction). This RNA-level resistance signal is real and independent of the VEZF1-TEAD1 biochemical claim -- it does not, by itself, confirm that TEAD1 regulates VEZF1.
verdict: DOWNGRADED FROM THE PRIOR PASS, PER CRITICAL VALIDATION: TEAD1 is NOT a validated indirect-targeting strategy for VEZF1 -- it is a druggable (pan-TEAD, not TEAD1-specific), project-evidence-aligned HYPOTHESIS worth testing (EXP-3), resting on a single cardiac/zebrafish paper that reports VEZF1 and TEAD-1 as binding partners at one promoter. TEAD1 WAS knocked down in that paper, but only as a co-IP antibody-specificity control, not to test a TEAD1->VEZF1 functional relationship -- so no perturbation evidence exists in either direction for that relationship specifically. NO breast-cancer or ER+ context of any kind, and NO other paper in PubMed connecting the two genes. This remains the most interesting available VEZF1 indirect-targeting candidate only because every other candidate examined is weaker still (correlation-only or wrong-direction) -- not because this candidate itself is strong in absolute terms.

candidate_x: p68RacGAP (possibly related to ARHGAP22, not independently confirmed)
regulates: physical binding partner of VEZF1 and Rac1; regulates the endothelin-1 promoter and endothelial tube formation
perturbation_type: functional GTPase assays + immunohistochemical/expression studies in the source paper; not a genetic knockdown/knockout of the GAP itself tested against VEZF1 output in that paper (i.e. binding is shown, but a perturbation-of-X-reduces-VEZF1-output experiment was not confirmed present)
druggability: RhoGAP-domain proteins are not a well-established small-molecule drug class in general; no specific inhibitor for this protein was identified in the searches performed
project_evidence: ARHGAP22 (the UniProt-listed VEZF1 interactor that may or may not be the same protein as 'p68RacGAP'): Hany CRISPR effect=-0.615, FDR=0.791 (not significant, sensitising_KO direction) -- from this project's own table; this figure is reported under the ARHGAP22 gene symbol specifically and its correspondence to 'p68RacGAP' is NOT confirmed
verdict: A REAL PHYSICAL INTERACTION, BUT DOES NOT CLEAR THE 'GENUINE PERTURBATION-BASED REGULATOR' BAR as strongly as TEAD1 -- reported as a secondary, lower-confidence lead requiring gene-identity confirmation before further use

regulates: VEZF1 protein stability (VEZF1 is a reported STUB1 ubiquitination substrate)
evidence_direction: STUB1 -> VEZF1 degradation (i.e. inhibiting STUB1 would be predicted to INCREASE, not decrease, VEZF1 -- the opposite of the desired direction for an indirect-inhibition strategy)
perturbation_type: reported in an HCC model (PMID 36241701, secondary-sourced -- primary full text was paywalled in both this pass and the prior phase)
druggability: STUB1/CHIP does not have a well-established clinical-stage small-molecule inhibitor
project_evidence: STUB1: Hany CRISPR effect=+0.029, FDR=0.993 (not significant, tolerance_associated_KO direction) -- from this project's own table
verdict: WRONG DIRECTION FOR AN INHIBITION STRATEGY -- inhibiting a protein that DEGRADES VEZF1 would be expected to increase, not decrease, VEZF1 levels; included for completeness/transparency, not as a viable lead
